clue.text: I can't forgive terrible shouting

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the preceding words are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to pardon awful yelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the twelve letters of I CANT FORGIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to vociferate is to cry out loudly and insistently.

clue.text: Criminal is proud about evil

indicators.note: one word is placed about the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: vain means proud, conceited
ill can mean evil or harm, as in 'speak ill of'

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer's arrogance surrounds their wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a villain is a wrongdoer or crook.

clue.text: Psalm uttered in church service finally

parts.note: oral means spoken, uttered

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word service

explanation.surface: A psalm is spoken aloud as a church service ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chorale is a hymn tune sung by a choir, and psalms are often sung in that form.

clue.text: Concentrating, not eating around middle of Lent

indicators.note: the word for not eating goes around the inserted letters

parts.note: fasting means going without food

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word Lent

explanation.surface: Someone focuses hard while abstaining from food in the middle of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: fastening on something, or fastening your attention, means focusing hard on it.

clue.text: Raiment often being exhibited with state openings

definitions.text: Raiment often being exhibited with state openings

indicators.note: openings are the starts of words, so take the first letter of each of the other words

explanation.surface: Ceremonial clothing is on show at state occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: robes are famously paraded at the State Opening of Parliament, Britain's annual ceremony where the monarch opens the parliamentary session. 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: robes are raiment, formal garments, worn by peers and the monarch at such ceremonies.

clue.text: Provoke Pooh's friend admitting Roo's first

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the friend's name takes a letter inside

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncing tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Roo

explanation.surface: Annoy Tigger by letting Roo in first.
explanation.walkthrough: Roo is also a Winnie-the-Pooh character, which keeps the surface in the Hundred Acre Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to trigger a reaction is to set it off or provoke it.

clue.text: Falls once more over uncovered trap

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, read upwards

parts.note: again means once more

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters off the word trap

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles again over an exposed trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AGAIN into NIAGA; 'uncovered' leaves RA from TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: Niagara Falls is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: St Cecilia sect almost converted minister

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of sect is dropped

explanation.surface: A saint's sect turned into a church minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SECT to SEC; 'converted' rearranges STCECILIA plus SEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ecclesiastic is a clergyman, a minister of the church.

clue.text: Label old American 'heartless'

parts.note: to call something is to name or label it
US stands for American, as in US citizens

explanation.surface: Branding an elderly American as unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: callous means unfeeling and cruel.

clue.text: Robber baron's beginning with purchasing outfit

indicators.note: purchasing means acquiring, so the outer letters take the outfit word in
beginning takes the first letter of baron

parts.note: and means with, together with
a rig is a set of clothes, an outfit

explanation.surface: A thieving baron starts by buying clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brigand is a bandit, especially one of a gang in the hills.

clue.text: Pass reduced commotion about parking permission

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter of the word for pass goes

parts.note: to pass away is to die

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for commotion goes round the parking letter

parts.note: a sensation is a stir, a commotion
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A ticket permitting parking is cut short amid a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' here means die, as in pass away; 'reduced' drops its last letter. 'about' wraps the commotion word round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dispensation is special permission, an exemption from a rule.

clue.text: Foliage irritation with sweetheart on meadow

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the irritation and sweetheart pieces follow the meadow

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
in British usage a fag is a tiresome chore, an irritation
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Leaves, an annoyance and a lover in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The British sense of fag as a tiresome chore is needed here, not the cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: leafage is the leaves of plants collectively, foliage.

clue.text: Cracked glass in making marks

indicators.note: cracked glass is broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Broken glass is leaving scratches.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: one event signals or marks the start of another.

clue.text: Seeing that transgression is followed by Church

indicators.note: is followed by puts the church letters after the transgression word

parts.note: a sin is a transgression, a moral offence
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An offence followed by churchgoing to atone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: since and seeing that both mean because.

clue.text: Painter facetiously assuming physical connection …

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: An artist jokingly adopting a bodily link, the ellipsis carrying on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an interface is a point where two systems or things meet and connect.

clue.text: Smashing ball or tee is not bad

indicators.note: smashing breaks things to pieces, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer hitting the ball off the tee hard does fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like British praise, which fits 'not bad', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tolerable means passable, acceptable, all right.

clue.text: … from clear change largely constraining Raphael?

indicators.note: constraining means holding in, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: a change from clarity largely restricting the painter Raphael.
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael looks like the Renaissance painter, which suits 'Painter' in the clue before, but here he is the angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example, hence the question mark: Raphael is one of the archangels in Jewish and Christian tradition.

clue.text: In clubs, date catching the man's fancy

indicators.note: catching means trapping, so the outer letters hold the pronoun inside

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
an era is a period, a date in history
the man gives him, the 's joining it to the rest

explanation.surface: At a nightclub, a date takes a man's fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a chimera is a wild fancy, an illusion of the imagination.

clue.text: A sailor reported storm

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the sound of the words is what counts

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, so a sailor gives a salt

explanation.surface: A seaman reports bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' looks like weather but is the verb, as in storming a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to storm a position is to attack it in a sudden violent rush.

clue.text: USA without Trump's lead provides satisfaction

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the States is a name for the USA

indicators.note: lead is the leading letter of the word Trump

explanation.surface: America minus its president is content.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that sates fully satisfies an appetite.

clue.text: Mobster thus managed to enter post office

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the managed word goes in the post office letters

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A gangster thereby got into the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: Tony Soprano is the mob boss in the TV series The Sopranos.

clue.text: Protection for most extreme members?

parts.note: members are limbs, and the parts at their very ends are the toes, so this is armour for toes

explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests radical activists, but here it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: toecaps are reinforced covers over the front of boots, guarding the toes at the body's extremities.

clue.text: Outfit isn't wet, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Clothes stay dry, to one's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper worn together, a classic British women's ensemble.

clue.text: City of Italy in fashion

indicators.note: in puts the Italy letter inside the fashion word

parts.note: to turn is to shape or fashion, as on a lathe
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian city that is stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City of Italy' reads as one definition, but 'Italy' is a wordplay piece, and 'in fashion' is not trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: Turin is a major city in north-west Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Most inferior tarts covered in mould

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped round, so the mould word goes round the tarts

parts.note: rot is decay, mould
tarts are pies, pastry cases with filling

explanation.surface: The worst pastries are coated in mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ropy is British slang for poor quality, so ropiest is the worst.

clue.text: Applaud taking Queen piece on board

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the applaud word holds the queen letters

parts.note: to cheer is to applaud

explanation.surface: Clapping when a chess queen captures a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: a chequer is a draughts piece, as in Chinese chequers or checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a chequer is a counter used in the board game draughts.

clue.text: Boasting from supporter with trouble accepting victory

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the outer words take the victory letter

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
ado is fuss, trouble
V stands for victory, as in V for Victory

explanation.surface: Swaggering talk from a fan who struggles to accept a win.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bravado is a show of boldness, swaggering bluster.

clue.text: Cross river docked by container ship

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the container and ship before the docked river

parts.note: a can is a container
a tanker is a ship carrying oil

indicators.note: docked means having its tail cut off, so the river loses its last letter

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A river crossing at a dock beside a container ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb about crossing the river, but it means angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cantankerous means bad-tempered and argumentative, like someone cross.
